moduleTitle: Module 1. Foundations, Membranes and Cell Signaling

competencies.name: Physiology and levels of function
competencies.can: Define physiology and place a given process at the correct level of organization from molecule to organism, then state the level at which that process is best explained.

competencies.name: Structure and function relationship
competencies.can: Predict how a change in the structure of a molecule, cell, tissue, or organ alters its function, using examples from two different organ systems.

competencies.name: Homeostasis defined
competencies.can: Define homeostasis, regulated variable, and setpoint, and distinguish homeostasis from chemical equilibrium and from steady state.

competencies.name: Feedback loop components
competencies.can: Diagram a negative feedback loop labeling stimulus, sensor, afferent path, integrating center, efferent path, effector, and response, and trace body temperature or blood glucose through every step.

competencies.name: Negative and positive feedback
competencies.can: Distinguish negative from positive feedback by the direction of the response and give a physiological example of each, explaining why a positive feedback loop needs an outside event to end it.

competencies.name: Feedforward control and acclimatization
competencies.can: Explain anticipatory feedforward control and acclimatization and identify which one is operating in a given scenario.

competencies.name: Local and reflex control pathways
competencies.can: Distinguish a local control pathway from a long distance reflex pathway and classify a given response as one or the other.

competencies.name: Mass balance
competencies.can: Apply the mass balance equation to a solute or to body water and calculate the intake, production, and output combination that holds the amount in the body constant.

competencies.name: Body fluid compartments
competencies.can: State the approximate volumes of total body water, intracellular fluid, extracellular fluid, plasma, and interstitial fluid in a 70 kg adult and compare the dominant solutes of the intracellular and extracellular compartments.

competencies.name: Compartment separation and clinical volume shifts
competencies.can: Predict the direction of water movement between compartments when extracellular osmolarity rises or falls and name a clinical situation that produces each shift.

competencies.name: Units and unit conversion
competencies.can: Convert among the units used in physiology including molarity, osmolarity, milliequivalents, mmHg, liters per minute, and percent solutions.

competencies.name: Graphing and data interpretation
competencies.can: Construct a labeled graph with the independent variable on the x axis, and read slope, direction, and trend from a physiological data set.

competencies.name: Experimental design and controls
competencies.can: Identify the hypothesis, independent variable, dependent variable, and control condition in a physiology experiment and state what the control rules out.

competencies.name: Measurement error and variability
competencies.can: Distinguish random from systematic error and explain why physiological measurements are repeated and averaged.

competencies.name: Water and solution properties
competencies.can: Explain how the polarity and hydrogen bonding of water determine solubility and identify whether a given solute is hydrophilic or hydrophobic.

competencies.name: pH and buffers
competencies.can: Define pH, state the normal pH range of arterial blood, and explain how a buffer pair resists a change in pH when acid or base is added.

competencies.name: Protein structure and function
competencies.can: Relate the levels of protein structure to binding site shape and explain how denaturation by heat or pH change destroys function.

competencies.name: Enzyme activity and regulation
competencies.can: Describe how enzymes lower activation energy and predict the effect of substrate concentration, temperature, pH, and competitive or allosteric inhibition on reaction rate.

competencies.name: ATP and energy coupling
competencies.can: Explain how ATP hydrolysis is coupled to endergonic cellular work and name three categories of work that require it.

competencies.name: Enzyme assay
competencies.can: Measure enzyme activity across a range of temperature or pH using a spectrophotometric or colorimetric assay, plot the results, and identify the optimum.

competencies.name: Membrane composition and fluidity
competencies.can: Describe the fluid mosaic membrane and state how phospholipids, cholesterol, glycolipids, and integral and peripheral proteins contribute to its properties.

competencies.name: Determinants of permeability
competencies.can: Rank molecules by their ability to cross a lipid bilayer unaided using size, charge, and lipid solubility, and predict which will require a protein.

competencies.name: Simple diffusion and Fick's law
competencies.can: State the variables in Fick's law of diffusion and predict how a change in concentration gradient, surface area, membrane thickness, or distance changes the rate of transfer.

competencies.name: Osmolarity and tonicity
competencies.can: Calculate the osmolarity of a solution, distinguish osmolarity from tonicity, and classify a solution as isotonic, hypotonic, or hypertonic to a cell.

competencies.name: Osmosis and cell volume
competencies.can: Predict the direction of water movement and the resulting change in cell volume when a cell is placed in a solution of stated osmolarity and penetrating solute content.

competencies.name: Diffusion and osmosis experiment
competencies.can: Measure diffusion and osmotic movement across a selectively permeable membrane and relate the observed rate to molecular size and concentration gradient.

competencies.name: Tonicity and red blood cells
competencies.can: Observe erythrocytes in solutions of different tonicity, identify crenation, normal shape, and hemolysis, and explain each result.

competencies.name: Facilitated diffusion
competencies.can: Describe carrier and channel mediated diffusion and explain why carrier mediated transport shows saturation and specificity while simple diffusion does not.

competencies.name: Primary active transport
competencies.can: Explain how the sodium potassium ATPase uses ATP to move three sodium out and two potassium in, and state the two gradients it maintains.

competencies.name: Secondary active transport
competencies.can: Distinguish symport from antiport and trace how the sodium gradient powers glucose uptake by SGLT and calcium removal by the sodium calcium exchanger.

competencies.name: Transport maximum and saturation
competencies.can: Interpret a transport rate curve, identify the transport maximum, and apply the concept to renal glucose handling in hyperglycemia.

competencies.name: Vesicular transport
competencies.can: Compare phagocytosis, pinocytosis, receptor mediated endocytosis, and exocytosis by trigger, cargo, and energy requirement.

competencies.name: Transepithelial transport
competencies.can: Trace glucose or sodium from lumen to blood across a polarized epithelium and identify which step occurs at the apical membrane and which at the basolateral membrane.

competencies.name: Transport simulation
competencies.can: Use a membrane transport simulation to distinguish simple diffusion from facilitated diffusion and active transport by their response to gradient reversal and metabolic poison.

competencies.name: Ion distribution and electrochemical gradients
competencies.can: State the typical intracellular and extracellular concentrations of sodium, potassium, chloride, and calcium and separate the chemical from the electrical component of the driving force on each ion.

competencies.name: Nernst equation
competencies.can: Calculate the equilibrium potential for an ion with the Nernst equation and explain what the sign of the result means for the direction that ion will move.

competencies.name: Resting membrane potential
competencies.can: Explain why the resting membrane potential sits near the potassium equilibrium potential and predict how it shifts when membrane permeability to potassium or sodium changes.

competencies.name: Ion channel gating
competencies.can: Compare leak, voltage gated, ligand gated, and mechanically gated channels by what opens each one and give a physiological location for each.

competencies.name: Depolarization and hyperpolarization
competencies.can: Define depolarization, repolarization, hyperpolarization, and overshoot and label each on a membrane potential tracing.

competencies.name: Membrane potential simulation
competencies.can: Manipulate extracellular potassium and sodium in a simulation and record the resulting change in resting membrane potential against the Nernst prediction.

competencies.name: Signal types and range
competencies.can: Classify a chemical signal as autocrine, paracrine, neurotransmitter, neurohormone, or hormone by its route and distance of travel.

competencies.name: Receptor location and ligand solubility
competencies.can: Predict whether a signal molecule binds a surface receptor or an intracellular receptor from its lipid solubility and relate that to the speed and duration of the response.

competencies.name: G protein coupled receptors
competencies.can: Trace a G protein coupled receptor pathway from ligand binding through the G protein and amplifier enzyme to the second messenger and the cellular response.

competencies.name: Second messengers
competencies.can: Identify cyclic AMP, IP3, diacylglycerol, and calcium as second messengers and state the enzyme that generates each and one target it activates.

competencies.name: Catalytic receptors and intracellular receptors
competencies.can: Compare a receptor enzyme such as the insulin receptor with an intracellular steroid receptor by mechanism and by time course of the response.

competencies.name: Signal amplification
competencies.can: Explain how a cascade amplifies a signal and estimate the size of the amplification across the steps of a given pathway.

competencies.name: Receptor modulation
competencies.can: Define agonist, antagonist, competitive inhibition, up regulation, and down regulation and predict the effect of chronic ligand excess on target cell sensitivity.

competencies.name: Signal termination
competencies.can: Name three mechanisms that end a chemical signal and explain why a signal that cannot be terminated produces pathology.

competencies.name: Dose response relationships
competencies.can: Plot a dose response curve, identify threshold, maximal response, and EC50, and compare a full agonist with a partial agonist on the same axes.
